title: Kemba's Step-Back Sinks Top-Seeded Pitt
dek: On UConn's third day in a row at the Garden, Kemba Walker crossed over Pitt center Gary McGhee, who fell, and swished a step-back jumper at the buzzer.

setup.text: UConn came to New York sliding. After a 10-0 start that included the Maui Invitational title, the Huskies lost four of their last five regular-season games, finished 9-9 in the Big East and drew the No. 9 seed: no bye, and five wins needed to take the title.
Kemba Walker, a first-team All-Big East guard, carried them through the first two days: 26 points in a 97-71 win over DePaul on Tuesday and 28 in a 79-62 rout of Georgetown on Wednesday.

Thursday's noon quarterfinal brought top-seeded Pittsburgh, 27-4 and ranked third in the country, playing its first game of the week after a double bye. The Panthers came in at plus-11 in rebounding margin, the best in the Big East.

game.text: Pitt started fast. Ashton Gibbs, who finished 10 of 13 with six 3-pointers and 27 points, helped build a 20-8 lead. Freshman Roscoe Smith took an elbow to the face with 7:20 left in the half; he needed eight stitches, never returned, and moments after he left UConn trailed 35-23.

Then freshman Shabazz Napier hit a 3 to start the rally. Jamal Coombs-McDaniel converted a three-point play, Walker scored six points in under two minutes, and UConn went ahead 40-39 on a Walker free throw with 6.1 seconds left in the half before Travon Woodall's twisting layup gave Pitt a 41-40 halftime lead.

The second half was a tug-of-war. Pitt pushed its lead to seven early; UConn took its first lead of the half at 61-60 on an Alex Oriakhi putback with 8:21 left, and the score was tied four more times before the final minute.
UConn won the hustle stats. It outrebounded the Big East's best rebounding team 32-25, including 17-9 on the offensive glass, and turned 11 Pitt turnovers into 20 points.

sequence.text: Pitt's Dante Taylor tips in a miss to tie the game.
Alex Oriakhi misses the first free throw and makes the second.
Shabazz Napier makes two free throws.
Brad Wanamaker answers with two free throws.
Walker misses a jumper, but Oriakhi grabs the rebound and puts it back in.
Ashton Gibbs comes free off a screen and hits a 3 from the corner, his sixth of the game, to tie it.
Walker drives past Wanamaker into an open look and comes up short. Jamal Coombs-McDaniel grabs the miss, only his second rebound of the game.

Coombs-McDaniel calls timeout. Jim Calhoun's play gives Walker two options: take the last shot himself or kick it to Coombs-McDaniel. Calhoun said it was built to get Walker matched up against Pitt's big man.

Walker gets the ball at the top of the key with about 15 seconds left and lets the clock run under five. Center Gary McGhee has switched onto him. A crossover and a shoulder roll put McGhee on the floor, and Walker steps back just inside the arc and swishes it as the buzzer sounds. Napier is the first to grab him and lift him into the air.

quotes.text: Everybody in the world knew that ball was coming to me. I wanted to take that shot.
I was going to go to the basket on him ... but he fell so I was able to get a clean look at the rim.
There wasn't any doubt in my mind what option it would be when he put the hard dribble down.
It was one of those games where Pittsburgh asks you, 'How tough are you? If you're tough enough, you can beat us.'

aftermath.text: The next night UConn beat No. 11 Syracuse 76-71 in overtime in the semifinals, with Walker scoring 33 points and grabbing 12 rebounds. On Saturday it beat No. 14 Louisville 69-66 for the program's seventh Big East tournament title, tying Georgetown for the most.
Walker was named the tournament's most valuable player. His 130 points broke the single-tournament record of 84 set by Syracuse's Eric Devendorf in 2009.
UConn then won six NCAA tournament games as a No. 3 seed, finishing with the national title on April 4.

legacy.text: It was the sixth game-winning shot of Walker's college career, according to SI, and the third of the 11 straight wins that closed UConn's 2011 championship season.
According to a 2026 Hartford Courant column, ESPN's Dave Pasch called it with Walker's nickname: 'Cardiac Kemba does it again.'

conflicts.ours: site has no play-by-play for 2011-33; the sequence uses UConn's official play-by-play, which logs it at 0:50
conflicts.source_says: AP: 'to knot it up with 47.9 seconds left'; SI: UConn 'led 74-71 with 50 seconds left' when Gibbs hit it

conflicts.ours: official play-by-play: UConn led 40-39 on Walker's free throw at 0:06; Woodall's layup at 0:01 made it Pitt 41-40 at the half
conflicts.source_says: SI: UConn went 'up 41-40 before a Travon Woodall layup gave the Panthers the lead back' (score misstated). Draft follows the official play-by-play and AP.

unsure: Dave Pasch as ESPN's play-by-play voice rests on a 2026 Hartford Courant column (via Yahoo Sports); the wording of his call differs between that column and a 2014 fan recollection, so the call is not quoted. The color analyst was not identified.
Gary McGhee's height: AP '6-foot-10', SI '6-11'. Not used.

Who set the screen that produced the switch: the 2026 Courant column says Coombs-McDaniel; SI (2011) says UConn set a screen at the top of the key and flared Coombs-McDaniel out for a possible 3. Draft doesn't name the screener.
AP says Napier was the first to grab Walker; SI describes Roscoe Smith, his face bandaged, practically carrying Walker off the court. Draft uses AP.

The site's videos[] for this game include buwdIsgizSs ('Uconn vs pitt', 62 s), whose description reads '2011 big east championship / March 11 2011' (UConn played Pitt on March 10). It could not be confirmed to show this game and is not included; consider dropping it from the game page too.
